result.summary:
Implemented contract C3: a stdlib-only scorer for the AIDB 2026 conformance/coverage protocol (Zhang, Tang, Ailamaki, sec. 3.2 eq. 1-3) applied to this repo's control variants, plus a unittest suite.

tools/aidb_scores.py
- CLI: --hardness H.json --throughput T.json --output S.json [--print] [--ddof 0|1] [--min-datasets 3] [--scope X (repeatable)]. Unknown options are rejected by argparse.
- Reads H = {dataset: {scope: {rmse, max_error, conflict_degree, pla_32, pla_4096}}} for any subset of scopes (full, full_flow, sample, sample_flow, sample_csv, sample_flow_csv; unknown scopes are also scored, after the canonical ones) and T = {variant: {dataset: mops_median}}.
- Writes S = {scope: {"metrics": {name: {"dims", "coverage", "conformance", "per_variant", "comparable_pairs", "incomparable_pairs", plus extras "per_variant_detail" (reward/penalty/counts) and "pairs" (ordered harder->easier comparable pairs and incomparable pairs), "alias":"GRE" on PLA-32·PLA-4096}}, "datasets", "variants", "skipped", "dropped_datasets", "ddof", "normalized_throughput", "hardness", "note"}}.
- All 25 metrics in canonical order: RMSE, ME, CD, PLA-32, PLA-4096, then the 10 two-dim and 10 three-dim compositions joined by the middle dot "·" in that component order (itertools.combinations preserves it).
- Protocol: p_hat = p / std over the scope's datasets (population std, ddof=0 default, documented in the module docstring; --ddof 1 = sample std; std 0 -> all p_hat 0, every gap 0, importance 0.5); harder-than partial order (>= on all dims, > on at least one; ties on every dim -> incomparable); a comparable pair is violating iff gap = p_hat(harder) - p_hat(easier) > 0, conforming iff gap <= 0; importance w = sigmoid(gap) (overflow-safe); Conf_I = (R-P)/(R+P), 0 when R+P == 0; Conf = mean over scored variants; Cov = (|C|-|U|)/(n choose 2).
- Dataset selection per scope: datasets with all five numeric fields in that scope's hardness block, intersected with every scored variant's throughput; a variant overlapping fewer than --min-datasets (3) is skipped with a "skipped: ..." reason in the output; datasets with missing/non-numeric fields are listed in dropped_datasets.
- --print renders a Table-2-like text table per scope (metric rows grouped scalar / two-dim / three-dim, one Conf_I column per variant, then Conf and Cov), with a footer stating these are reduced-scale, single-host, clean-room controls and not a reproduction of Table 2.

tests/test_aidb_scores.py (17 tests, unittest, no binary needed)
- Hand-built 4-dataset example (a,b,c,d; RMSE 1,2,3,4; ME 1,3,2,4; throughput 4,2,3,1) with the full arithmetic in comments: std = sqrt(1.25); p_hat = 3.57771/1.78885/2.68328/0.89443; the six RMSE pairs' gaps and sigmoid weights; R = 0.93079, P = 0.70980 (one violating pair c>b), Conf_RMSE = 0.13470, Cov = 1; RMSE·ME makes (b,c) incomparable -> Cov = 4/6, P = 0, Conf = 1; RMSE·ME·CD with CD tied everywhere equals RMSE·ME; CD alone -> Cov = -1, Conf = 0; ddof=1 changes scale not sign.
- Properties: every scalar metric has Cov = 1 when values are distinct (20 random corpora); adding a dimension never increases coverage (30 random distinct-valued corpora, all 2-dim vs their scalars and all 3-dim vs their 2-dim subsets); a perfectly conforming ordering gives Conf_I = 1 and a reversed one -1 on all 25 metrics (Conf = 0 as their mean); equal throughput -> all conforming with importance 0.5; sigmoid sign/monotonicity/overflow; canonical 25 names and GRE alias.
- Dataset selection: variants with < 3 overlapping datasets are skipped and reported; dataset set is the intersection across scored variants; scopes are independent and a dataset with missing fields is dropped for that scope only.
- CLI end to end via subprocess: --print output, --ddof 1, nested output dir creation, contract keys on all 25 metrics, conformance == mean of per_variant; unknown option and no-usable-scope both exit non-zero.

findings.description: Documented contract deviation, confirmed material: default_ut_epsilon<double>() replaces LIPP's absolute +1e-6 on U_T with 1e-6 * (range/(n-1)) for the transformed and smoothed blocks, so those CD values are NOT what a literal LIPP FMCD fit would give on the same features. findings.description: CD is rounding-decided for keys whose predicted position lies within one double ulp of an integer slot boundary (FmcdModel::predict evaluates a*(key-anchor)+base in double, as LIPP evaluates a*key+b in floating point). On the real books 2M sample the CLI reports CD 11 while an exact-rational evaluation of the identical model (same D, U_T, capacity, a, b) gives 10; on an adversarial dense cluster the gap is 1.7%. This is not a port error (emulating LIPP's own a*key+b in double also gives 11) but CD is not bit-reproducible across arithmetic, which the report should acknowledge when it ranks datasets by CD.
findings.evidence: scratch oracle on data/samples/books_2M_uniform_s42: D cpp=10 py=10, U_T cpp=py=2300186144265.4873, L=4000000 identical; CD cpp-emulated=11 (slot 3999999 = L-1) , lipp-double=11, exact-rational=10 (the +1e-6 on U_T is below double resolution at U_T~2.3e12, so keys[size-1-D] lands exactly on L-1 in double but just below it exactly). Position ulp near 3999999 = 4.66e-10 vs per-unit-key increment a = 4.35e-13 -> keys within ~1071 of a boundary are rounding-decided. Adversarial scratch/fallback7 (150k sparse keys 3e9 apart + 150k consecutive keys at 9e18, fallback branch): CLI 101104, exact-rational 99439, plain double 102383. All other 12 datasets (fixture 129, near_u64 4, fallback5 1000, fb 5M prefix 94, ...) agree exactly.
findings.suggested_fix: Either document in hardness.hpp and the report that CD carries +-1 (typical) arithmetic uncertainty, or make the slot assignment canonical by evaluating floor(a*(key-anchor)+base) with an exact rational/fixed-point comparison at the boundary (e.g. compute the slot with __int128 arithmetic on a's exact mantissa) so CD no longer depends on the platform's rounding.

Threshold at which the flow stops being chosen, c* = min(binary, raw, vp_raw) - (vp_flow - 4), on the 10 datasets where the flow was chosen: planet_window 4.13, covid_window 4.15, genome_window 4.22, covid_uniform 4.63, history_window 4.91, stack_window 5.10, libio_window 5.40, fb_window 5.96, books_window 5.97, wise_window 6.25 (flow+ranks candidates are never competitive, c* < 0). findings.claim: C6: The slowdown of the flow-fused root is attributable to the transform evaluation (transform_calls per lookup > 0 only in those runs), not to extra probes or memory.
findings.evidence: Supported in substance, wrong in the parenthetical. transform_calls/lookup T equals root_flow + flow_regions/regions to within 0.0015 on every run: T = 1.000-1.035 in the 60 runs with root_flow=true, but T is also > 0 (0.0006-0.088, from region-level flow accepted in 0.2-8.8% of regions) in 90 other runs (packed_rank_root_flow on all 20 datasets, root_fusion and vp10_root_fusion where raw+fences was chosen), and those runs show no slowdown (root_flow fallback vs packed_rank: dns = -3.5 +- 27 ns, mean ratio +1.1%). Dose-response: the +46.7 ns [40, 53] loss appears in exactly the T~1 pairs; the 45 raw-feature model-root pairs (T = 0) gain 4.1 ns per probe saved; the 75 sham pairs (identical code path) give -0.9 +- 21.7 ns. Not extra probes: root probes fall by 4.2-6.4 per lookup and every other work counter (fence_probes, coordinate_probes, delta_probes, key_at_calls, decoded_keys, codec_bytes_examined, block_routes, correction_distance) is identical to packed_rank on the same (dataset, seed) for all root variants and for vp10_root_fusion vs vp10 (max abs difference 0.000 per lookup), so decoding work is unchanged. Not memory: metadata_bytes of the flow-root runs exceed packed_rank by exactly 4*(regions + root_virtual) = 7,312-8,780 bytes (the slot table; 0.004 B/key; key/value bytes identical), while raw+fences roots on uniform samples carry 1,960-9,780-byte tables (osm/planet 1,956 slots) and gain 0-16%; a regression of dns on slot-table size among the 81 raw+fences pairs gives +0.9 ns/KB [-13, +8.5], i.e. no detectable table-size effect, and every root structure (489 fences, <= 2,445 uint32 slots, 144-byte flow) is L1-resident. Not noise: mean -11.6% over 60 pairs with sd 6.3% (t = 12) against a sham mean of +0.3% (sd 5.8%), run order randomized. Not a window-sample artefact: covid_uniform, the one uniform sample with a flow root, loses the same 15% (0.848), while the sham pairs on window samples show no dataset-type bias. Mechanism consistent: transform() (transform.hpp:61-77) does (key-mean)/var, floor, two 2x2 matmuls and two std::tanh through a non-inlined pointer call with runtime loop bounds; its build-loop cost is 28.2 +- 2.2 ns/key, so ~66 ns on the latency-bound lookup chain is plausible. What the data cannot do: the counters are software counters, so the 66 ns is 'the flow-feature root path minus the raw-feature root path' by elimination; it cannot separate the tanh arithmetic from a possibly different branch-misprediction profile of the exponential search started from the flow-predicted slot (that alternative would need the 2.6-4.8 remaining probes to cost 13-22 ns each against the 4 ns measured for raw-feature probes, which is implausible but not excluded), and the raw-feature model roots that anchor the 4 ns/probe all sit on uniform samples.
findings.correction: Write: 'transform_calls per lookup is ~1.0 only when the selector chose the flow feature at the root (0.0006-0.09 elsewhere, from the region-level flow, with no measurable effect); those 60 runs and only those lose 47 ns [40, 53] per lookup (-11.6%), with every non-root work counter identical to the baseline and a metadata difference equal to the 7-9 KB slot table, which raw-feature roots of the same size carry at a net gain. The attribution to the flow evaluation is by elimination and dose-response (software counters), consistent with its 28 ns/key build-loop cost; a hardware profile would be needed to separate tanh cost from branch behaviour of the flow-fed exponential search.'

findings.claim: C1 headline / the word 'synergy': on the window samples each single candidate (raw, flow, fences) is worse than binary while the fusion beats it, because the transform removes whole-range curvature that the virtual fences cannot express.
findings.evidence: The as-built numbers stand (see the (a)-(d) findings) but the mechanism does not. Region 0's low_fence is the sentinel 0 (index.hpp:429 `r->low_fence=i?rows[i].first:0`), and fit_root fits the raw root on all 489 fences with origin=fences[0]=0, span=last fence (model.hpp fit_xy). For a contiguous window the first real key sits at 95.6-99.9% of that span (sentinel gap fraction: books_window 0.970, covid 0.999, fb 0.989, genome 0.994, history 0.989, libio 0.990, osm 0.998, planet 0.956, stack 0.989, wise 0.995), so 488 fences collapse to x~1 and the sentinel is a leverage point: the OLS root predicts rank ~244 for every real key. Signature in the data: raw residuals on 8/10 windows are identical to two digits (rms 139.5-140.7 regions, median ~121, max ~242, 0% of fences within one region), and the stored raw estimate is 14.14-14.38 on all ten windows regardless of dataset. Counterfactual with an exact Python emulation of fit_root's estimator (reproduces every stored binary/raw/flow estimate on all 20 samples to the printed digits): fitting the raw root on the 488 real fences (origin = first real fence; region 0 still present and probed) gives raw+ranks = books 2.32, wise 2.99, fb 3.58, libio 3.63, history 3.85, covid 6.14, stack 6.29, genome 7.26, planet 7.59, osm 10.55, i.e. below binary (8.96) on 9/10 windows with no flow and no fences, and on books/wise/fb/libio/history at or below the fusion's measured 2.93/2.56/2.88/3.48/3.91. What the flow contributes as built is its own input normalization x=(k-mean)/var with the window's mean/std followed by tanh saturation, which compresses the sentinel to a bounded outlier; the fences then work on top of it. The same artifact produces the only uniform 'synergy' case: covid_uniform has sentinel gap 0.930 and its raw root goes 13.78 -> 4.63 without the sentinel (wise_uniform, gap 0.50: 6.54 -> 5.75; all other uniform samples, gap < 0.04: unchanged to 0.03).

Memory: metadata +0.003-0.004 B/key (0.571 -> 0.574). Total probes are 23-39% lower, so 'not extra probes or memory' holds; attribution to the transform is by elimination and dose-response (no hardware profile).
